title: New York's 6th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: New York's 6th congressional district, covering central and eastern Queens neighborhoods including Flushing, Jackson Heights, Elmhurst, and Forest Hills, is holding a U.S. House election in 2026. Incumbent Democrat Grace Meng, first elected in 2012 and re-elected with 60.7% in 2024, faces a primary challenge from former U.S. diplomat Chuck Park, who is running on a progressive platform including abolishing ICE and universal healthcare. On the Republican side, Joseph Chou is running unopposed in the primary after Juan Pagan withdrew. The district has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+6, and the Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid D' as of February 2025, though the district swung 24 points toward Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election, indicating potential competitiveness.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found for this race. Prediction market data from City & State NY shows Grace Meng leading the Democratic primary at 85% odds versus Chuck Park at 11%, but this is not a scientific poll.

candidates.name: Grace Meng
candidates.summary: Grace Meng is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 6th congressional district, first elected in 2012. She is the first Asian American elected to Congress from New York and serves on the House Appropriations Committee. Meng faces a primary challenge from Chuck Park in the 2026 Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Chuck Park
candidates.summary: Chuck Park is a former U.S. Foreign Service diplomat and former chief of staff to New York City Councilmember Shekar Krishnan. Born in Flushing to Korean immigrant parents, he is challenging incumbent Grace Meng in the Democratic primary on a progressive platform that includes abolishing ICE, universal healthcare, and opposing a casino in Queens.
